coaching_notes: Choosing the right entry model depends on market conditions, the quality of the order block, and your personal risk tolerance.
The stronger and cleaner the order block, the more aggressive the entry model you can justify.
In weaker or more volatile environments, conservative entries offer greater protection and consistency.
Most traders who believe they understand order blocks are actually losing money using them because they don't correctly identify a true institutional order block.
A mitigated order block no longer represents unfilled institutional interest; it becomes significantly weaker and should not be relied on for future entries.
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: bullish market context confirmed by a break of structure (price breaks above the previous major high)
PRECONDITION (OB definition): order block is the last bearish candle before a strong upward displacement that breaks structure
VALIDATION 1 (liquidity sweep): final bearish candle breaks the low of the previous candle and immediately reverses upward
VALIDATION 2 (imbalance/FVG): impulsive reversal creates a fair value gap above the order block; non-overlapping candles
VALIDATION 2 exception: if no imbalance forms above the sweep candle, extend the order block boundary to include the next candle and require imbalance above that candle
VALIDATION 3 (unmitigated): price must not have returned into the zone; a wick dropping into the zone during formation mitigates and invalidates it
ENTRY TRIGGER: price retraces into the order block and a change-of-character (break of an internal low) acts as the entry trigger (not a reversal signal)
ENTRY MODEL A: buy limit at upper wick of OB candle
ENTRY MODEL B: buy limit at upper body of OB candle
ENTRY MODEL C: buy limit at midpoint of OB zone
STOP LOSS: just below the lower wick of the order-block candle, adjusted by the spread
TIMEFRAME: 15-minute execution chart (USDJPY worked example)
consensus_scopes.entry_summary: In a bullish structure (price breaks the previous major high = break of structure), identify a valid institutional order block: the last bearish candle before a strong upward displacement that (1) performs a liquidity sweep (final bearish candle breaks the previous candle's low then immediately reverses up), (2) has imbalance/fair value gap forming above it (extend the OB boundary to the next candle if the sweep candle itself shows no imbalance), and (3) remains unmitigated (price has not yet returned into the zone). When price retraces back into the order block (a change-of-character / internal-low break acts as the entry trigger), place a buy limit order to fill inside the zone. Entry price within the zone depends on the chosen entry model (upper wick / upper body / midpoint).
consensus_scopes.exit_summary: Stop loss placed just below the lower wick of the order-block candle, adjusted by the spread. Take profit is discussed only as a risk-to-reward tradeoff (aggressive entries give better R:R, conservative entries lower R:R) with no concrete profit target given.
consensus_scopes.name: institutional_order_block_reversal_entry
